jobs.prompt:
FILE ACCESS: your declared outputs are readable. Train 8 owner gate: a 1-hour soak with the Command Center dashboard open. After bounding the 1 s live detector to 6 roots, the 10-minute soak still showed 14% average server CPU (limit 5%) with RSS and browser heap flat. Cause: every request older than the 60 s snapshot TTL starts a full board rebuild; on this machine that rebuild takes ~3 s and scans 441 project-family roots, and it runs every minute even when nothing changed.

Fix in tools/watch-server.mjs: keep the 60 s TTL and stale-while-revalidate, but make the FULL rebuild change-driven and add a deep backstop.
- Add a `changesSinceFullRebuild` flag. Set it whenever the 1 s detector reports changed project ids (both in updateCommandCenterChanges and in the rebuild's own scan). Reset it when a full rebuild starts (so changes that arrive during the rebuild set it again for the next cycle).
- Add a createWatchServer option `snapshotMaxStaleMs = 120000` (tests override it). In commandCenterResponse, when the cache is at/over snapshotTtlMs: start a background rebuild only if `changesSinceFullRebuild` is true, or the cache age is at/over snapshotMaxStaleMs. If neither, serve the cached entry (and its validators) without rebuilding. A cold cache still builds immediately; stale responses still return at once while a rebuild runs in the background; the live patch path is unchanged. This keeps the 60 s cache for changes and a 2-minute deep refresh for inputs the live detector does not watch (idle family roots, machine totals).
- Do not change the incremental live patch, the SSE path, the 60 s TTL itself, security headers, tokens/cookies or ETag/304 handling.

Tests in tests/command-center-perf-budget.test.mjs:
- Update the existing 'one snapshot shares Hive, Cockpit and arbitrary queries for 60 seconds, then serves stale and refreshes' test: at 60 s with no changed input, assert no new full build (reads unchanged) and the stale/304 response still works; then advance to snapshotMaxStaleMs (pass `snapshotMaxStaleMs: 120000` to the fixture server) and assert exactly one rebuild. Rename/reword it to describe the deep refresh.
- Update 'stale Hive and Cockpit return without waiting for a single background rebuild' so the background rebuild is triggered by a real changed input OR by advancing to snapshotMaxStaleMs; keep asserting the stale response beats the rebuild.
- Add a test: when a watched project input changes (write the fixture project's .swarm/project/tickets.json after the first build), the first request after the 60 s TTL triggers a rebuild; when nothing changes, it does not before snapshotMaxStaleMs.
- Keep every existing test green (run the whole file).

Verify: node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/command-center-perf-budget.test.mjs tests/command-center-live.test.mjs tests/command-center-soak.test.mjs tests/watch-server.test.mjs -> all pass. Report the rebuild counts and how you proved the idle path does not rebuild.
